claims.text: In as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys, magnetocaloric response is governed by nanoscale chemical ordering and defect-induced internal strain.
In as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi alloys, magnetic hysteresis is governed by nanoscale chemical ordering and defect-induced internal strain.
A higher deposition rate produces greater atomic disorder.
A higher deposition rate increases defect density.
Greater atomic disorder and defect density broaden the first-order magnetostructural transition.
Broadening or moderating the first-order magnetostructural transition reduces hysteresis losses under low applied fields.
The disorder-induced broadening of the transition lowers the peak magnetic entropy change.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal state.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi alloy contains deposition-induced microstructural inhomogeneities.
Deposition rate can be varied during sputter synthesis while other processing parameters are held constant.
Changing deposition rate changes the balance between atomic ordering and defect formation.
Increased disorder creates a broader distribution of local transition temperatures.
Higher-rate samples will have a broader magnetic transition than lower-rate or baseline samples.
Higher-rate samples will have lower hysteresis losses than lower-rate or baseline samples during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Lower-rate samples will retain a sharper transition and a higher peak entropy change.
Conventional-rate as-deposited samples show a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition, high hysteresis, and a large abrupt magnetocaloric entropy change.
The proposed deposition-rate relationship holds within the non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi composition window and practically achievable sputter-deposition rates.
The proposed relationship may not apply to bulk-cast or thermomechanically processed forms that undergo extensive atomic reordering.
